taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit: a low spring herb with basal leaves and a leafless flowering stalk.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name; wcvp_names.csv of the v16 zip, read 2026-10-17).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "scape rather stout, 25-45 cm. long, 1-several-flowered".

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "Corm narrowly oblong, 3-4 cm. long, arising in succession from the rhizome": a perennial.

traits.perennation.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "Corm narrowly oblong, 3-4 cm. long, arising in succession from the rhizome".

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 426, Erythronium: "the stem simple, bearing two broad or narrow unequal leaves, usually below the middle, the leaves thus appearing basal".

traits.leaf_habit.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 426, Erythronium: "Low herbaceous plants, from deep-seated membranous-coated corms", dying back after flowering.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "Leaves not mottled, oblong-ovate".

traits.leaf_apex.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "acute or acutish at apex, abruptly narrowed at base".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FNA vol. 26 (eFloras), Erythronium montanum: "Leaves 10–20 cm"; Abrams (1923 p. 428): leaves "7-12 cm. long"; drawn 7 cm to 15 cm, 20 cm the rare high.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: leaves "2.5-4 cm. wide".

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "petiole 3-5 cm. long".

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 426, Erythronium: "Flowers large, nodding, bractless, solitary or in few-several-flowered racemes".

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: One to three flowers to a scape; Abrams (1923 p. 428): "1-several-flowered", set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 7199833, 3235549, 89350561, 109882672, 302223287, 145483889, 124825712, 145506538): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_posture.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 426, Erythronium: "Flowers large, nodding".

traits.perianth_reflexion.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: perianth-segments "somewhat recurved".

traits.tepal_length_m.note: FNA vol. 26 (eFloras), Erythronium montanum: tepals "broadly ovate to broadly lanceolate, 25–45 mm"; Abrams (1923 p. 428): "35-40 mm. long, 10-13 mm. wide".

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: open flowers 5.5 cm to 7.5 cm across their somewhat recurved 35-40 mm tepals, as in the photos.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "perianth-segments white with an orange base, often drying pinkish"; sRGB by eye.

traits.perianth_base_colour.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "white with an orange base"; sRGB by eye from the photos (golden orange).

traits.perianth_base_length.note: The orange base about a fifth of each tepal, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 7199833, 3235549, 89350561, 109882672, 302223287, 145483889, 124825712, 145506538): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.anther_colour.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "anthers white, 3-4 mm. long"; drawn cream, as the pollen colours them in the photos.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "capsule oblong-obovate, rounded at the apex".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: capsule "about 3 cm. long".

traits.flowering_months.note: In flower in July and August on Mount Rainier, as the snow melts, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 7199833, 3235549, 89350561, 109882672, 302223287, 145483889, 124825712, 145506538): the sources read give no count or measure.

generator.params.note: Yellow trout lily's (erythronium-americanum) values, changed by hand for avalanche lily: two basal leaves under a taller, stouter leafless scape (Abrams 1923 p. 428: "scape rather stout, 25-45 cm. long, 1-several-flowered") with about two large nodding white flowers on short stalks. Not fitted to measurements. flower_angle corrected from 110 to 140 (2026-10-19), as glacier lily's, so the flowers hang: Abrams (1923 p. 426), Erythronium: "Flowers large, nodding"; FNA vol. 26 gives E. montanum's tepals as recurved from a nodding flower.

appearance.organs.basal.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "Leaves not mottled, oblong-ovate, 7-12 cm. long, 2.5-4 cm. wide"; "petiole 3-5 cm. long". The template's mottling removed, the blade broader and stalked.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 428, Erythronium montanum: "perianth-segments white with an orange base", "somewhat recurved". Drawn white with a golden-orange centre, the tepals curled back less than the glacier lily's.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: two broad, plain green basal leaves under a stout leafless stalk carrying one to three nodding white lilies with golden-orange centres. Organ cards from yellow trout lily's (erythronium-americanum), recoloured and resized by hand. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

allometry.note: 0.32 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows in subalpine parkland. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from Abrams and FEIS, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from a built-in template.
